cases.title: Core - User - My Orders - Add single item to digital wallet
cases.description: Verify that a buyer can add one eligible order item from My Orders to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet, including NFC tickets that use the authenticated Google Wallet flow.
cases.preconditions:
A buyer has an order with exactly one eligible item that exposes digital wallet passes.
The item is activated, paid or usable, not transferred, not listed for resale, and has barcode/pass data available.
For NFC Google Wallet coverage, the buyer is logged in and the order contains one eligible NFC pass-only ticket.
Use a compatible OS/browser for the wallet type being tested.
cases.postconditions: The pass is available in the native wallet and the order item remains accessible from My Orders.

steps.action: Open My Orders and select an order with exactly one eligible wallet item.
steps.expected_result: The order details page loads for the selected order.

steps.action: Verify the Add to Wallet action for the detected wallet provider.
steps.expected_result: The Apple Wallet or Google Wallet action is visible and enabled for the item. For logged-in NFC Google Wallet coverage, the Google Wallet action is available from order details.

steps.action: Click the Add to Wallet action.
steps.expected_result: The platform wallet save flow opens without a Showpass UI error.

steps.action: When running the NFC Google Wallet variant, observe the redirected Google Wallet save flow.
steps.expected_result: The Google Wallet save page or provider flow opens with expected pass data and no Showpass UI error.

steps.action: Complete or simulate the provider flow to save the pass.
steps.expected_result: The pass is saved to the native wallet or provider confirmation page.

steps.action: Open the saved pass and review the pass details.
steps.expected_result: The event, item, date/time, venue, ticket holder, and seat details are accurate for the order item.

cases.title: Core - User - My Orders - Exchanges - Verify Barcode Handling (Visibility and NFC Interaction) During Exchange Process
cases.description: This Core test verifies the behavior of barcodes (standard and NFC-based) associated with an item (e.g. an event ticket within an order) while an exchange is in progress and after it's completed. It ensures barcodes are appropriately hidden or invalidated to prevent misuse, applicable across platforms supporting exchanges for orders. This is not specific to resale.
cases.preconditions:
1. Exchange functionality is enabled for the event/product.
2. An order exists with items that have associated barcodes (e.g., tickets). One item is an NFC-enabled event ticket.
3. The user can normally view their order barcodes (e.g., on 'My Orders' page, ticket PDF, or digital wallet pass).
cases.postconditions:
1. When an exchange is initiated for an item, its associated barcode (visual and data for NFC) becomes hidden, clearly marked as "Exchange in Progress", or otherwise invalidated.
2. For NFC tickets, any rotating barcode value should not be available or should indicate an invalid state during an exchange.
3. After a successful exchange, the barcode for the original item is permanently invalidated.
4. The new item received from the exchange receives a new, valid barcode.

steps.action: User purchases an item with a barcode (e.g., an event ticket, one of which is NFC-enabled).
steps.expected_result: Barcode is visible and active. NFC value is available and pass can be added to wallet.

steps.action: View the barcode for the item (e.g., in My Orders, on ticket PDF, or NFC pass in wallet). Note its state/visibility. For NFC, note if value is active.
steps.expected_result: Barcode and NFC pass are in their normal, active state.

steps.action: Initiate an exchange for this item. Do not complete it yet.
steps.expected_result: Exchange process starts. The original item is marked for exchange.

steps.action: While the exchange is in progress (before completion), check the barcode status for the original item again (e.g., in My Orders, attempt to view PDF/NFC pass).
steps.expected_result: The barcode for the original item is hidden, shows "Exchange in Progress", or is otherwise marked as temporarily invalid. NFC value for original ticket is unavailable/invalid; attempting to view/add the original NFC pass shows an error or "exchange in progress" status.

steps.action: Complete the exchange successfully, receiving a new item.
steps.expected_result: Exchange completes successfully. The original item is removed/replaced, and a new item is added to the order/inventory.

steps.action: Check the barcode status for the original item post-exchange. Attempt to use/view it.
steps.expected_result: The barcode for the original item is permanently invalidated and cannot be used for entry. Any associated NFC pass is also invalidated. Attempts to view or use it confirm its invalid status.

steps.action: Check the barcode for the new item received from the exchange.
steps.expected_result: The new item has a new, valid barcode. If it's an NFC item, it has a new, valid NFC pass that can be added to a wallet and used for entry.

cases.title: Core - User - Upcoming - NFC - Verify wallet button is absent from ticket list
cases.description: Verify that NFC tickets on the Upcoming ticket list do not expose an Add to Google Wallet action directly from the list item.
cases.preconditions:
A buyer has purchased an NFC-enabled event ticket.
The buyer is viewing the Upcoming tickets list.
cases.postconditions: The Upcoming list does not provide the NFC wallet action directly.

steps.action: Navigate to the Upcoming tickets page.
steps.expected_result: The Upcoming page loads with purchased future tickets.

steps.action: Locate an NFC ticket in the list.
steps.expected_result: The NFC ticket is visible in the Upcoming list.

steps.action: Inspect the actions available on the NFC ticket list item.
steps.expected_result: No Add to Google Wallet action is visible or actionable from the list item; wallet access is reached from order details when eligible.

cases.title: Web Public - Post Purchase - Verify Add to Digital Wallet Functionality from Thank You Screen
cases.description: Verifies that a user can successfully add their purchased tickets to a digital wallet (e.g., Apple Wallet, Google Pay) from the 'Thank You' page and that the ticket information in the wallet is correct.
cases.preconditions:
- Buyer completes checkout for an event ticket that supports digital wallet delivery.
- The purchase reaches the thank-you page.
- Test device or browser can open the selected wallet provider flow.
cases.postconditions:
- Wallet action remains available only for supported ticket types.
- Added pass details match the purchased ticket and order.
- Thank-you page remains accessible after returning from the wallet flow.

steps.action: Complete a ticket purchase for an event that supports digital wallet integration, using a compatible device/browser.
steps.expected_result: Purchase is successful and the 'Thank You' screen is displayed.

steps.action: Locate and click the 'Add to Apple Wallet' or 'Add to Google Pay' (or similar) button on the 'Thank You' screen.
steps.expected_result: The digital wallet pass file (.pkpass or similar) is downloaded, or the respective wallet application is invoked.

steps.action: Follow the prompts to add the ticket(s) to the digital wallet.
steps.expected_result: The ticket(s) are successfully added to the digital wallet.

steps.action: Open the digital wallet application and view the added ticket(s).
steps.expected_result: The ticket(s) are visible in the wallet.

steps.action: Verify the information displayed on the digital wallet pass: event name, date, time, venue, seat information (if applicable), QR code/barcode, and any other relevant details.
steps.expected_result: All information on the digital pass is accurate and matches the purchased ticket details.

cases.title: Core - User - Wallet - Verify assigned seating details on Apple and Google Wallet passes
cases.description: Verifies that a buyer can add an assigned-seating ticket to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet and that the generated pass displays the correct event and seat details.
cases.preconditions:
- Buyer has purchased an assigned-seating event ticket.
- The event is configured to support digital wallet passes.
- Test device or wallet test path is available for the selected wallet provider.
cases.postconditions:
- Wallet pass is created without duplicate stale passes.
- Pass details match the purchased ticket.
- Buyer can still open the original ticket details from the account or order surface.

steps.action: Open the purchased assigned-seating ticket from the buyer account or order detail page.
steps.expected_result: Ticket details load and show the assigned section, row, seat, event date/time, and venue.

steps.action: Select the add-to-wallet action for the selected wallet provider.
steps.expected_result: Wallet provider flow opens or generates the pass successfully.

steps.action: Open the generated wallet pass.
steps.expected_result: The pass opens without an error and belongs to the purchased ticket.

steps.action: Compare the pass details with the ticket detail page and order data.
steps.expected_result: Event name, venue, date/time, barcode/pass identifier, section, row, and seat match the purchased ticket.

steps.action: Return to the ticket detail page and confirm the ticket remains accessible.
steps.expected_result: The original ticket detail page still opens and no duplicate or stale wallet state is shown.

cases.title: Core - User - My Orders - NFC - Verify Digital Wallet Pass Generation and Data Accuracy for NFC Ticket (Non-Resold)
cases.description: Verifies that for an NFC-enabled event ticket (not listed for resale), the system correctly generates data for a digital wallet pass (e.g., Google Wallet, Apple Wallet) and that this pass contains accurate event and ticket information and NFC-specific properties.
cases.preconditions: User has purchased an NFC-enabled event ticket (not listed for resale).|||The event and venue are configured for NFC.|||User is attempting to add the NFC ticket to their digital wallet.
cases.postconditions: A digital wallet pass is generated successfully for the NFC ticket.|||The pass contains accurate information: event name, date, time, venue, ticket holder name, seat information (if applicable).|||The pass is configured for NFC tap-and-go (e.g., contains the necessary NFC payload or reference).|||The pass does NOT display a static, scannable barcode/QR code if the NFC implementation relies solely on tap or rotating codes.

steps.action: User navigates to 'My Orders' and selects an NFC ticket.
steps.expected_result: NFC ticket is selected.

steps.action: User initiates the 'Add to Wallet' (Google/Apple) action for the NFC ticket.
steps.expected_result: 'Add to Wallet' action is triggered.

steps.action: System generates the pass data.
steps.expected_result: Pass data is generated without error.

steps.action: User (or test system) inspects the content and properties of the generated digital pass.
steps.expected_result: All event and ticket details on the pass are accurate. The pass is identifiable as an NFC pass (e.g., specific fields, instructions). No static barcode is visible if per NFC rules. The pass successfully loads into the wallet app.

cases.title: Core - User - My Orders - NFC - Verify Confirmation Communication Content for NFC Event Purchase
cases.description: Ensures that order confirmation communications (e.g., email) for purchases including NFC event tickets clearly indicate the NFC nature of the tickets and provide appropriate instructions or information.
cases.preconditions: User purchases one or more tickets for an NFC-enabled event.
cases.postconditions: The order confirmation email (and any other relevant confirmation communication) is sent to the user.|||The communication explicitly mentions that the tickets are NFC-enabled / digital tap-and-go passes.|||Instructions on how to add the NFC pass to a digital wallet are clear and accurate.|||The communication de-emphasizes or omits references to printable PDF tickets or static barcodes if they are not the primary entry method for these NFC tickets.

steps.action: User completes a purchase for an NFC event.
steps.expected_result: Purchase is successful.

steps.action: User receives and opens the order confirmation email.
steps.expected_result: Confirmation email is received.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the email, focusing on how the NFC tickets are described and what actions are suggested.
steps.expected_result: The email content clearly states that the tickets are NFC digital passes. Verbiage like "Add to Apple Wallet" or "Save to Google Wallet" is prominent. Information about using the phone for entry via NFC is present. There is no 'Download PDF tickets' button or attachment for the NFC tickets, or it's clearly marked as not for entry.

cases.title: Core - User - My Orders - Add multiple items to digital wallet
cases.description: Verify that a buyer can add wallet passes for an order with multiple eligible items from My Orders.
cases.preconditions:
A buyer has an order with two or more eligible wallet items.
The items are activated, paid or usable, not transferred, not listed for resale, and have barcode/pass data available.
Use compatible wallet contexts for Apple Wallet or Google Wallet.
cases.postconditions: The buyer can save passes for the intended eligible items in the order.

steps.action: Open the order details page for an order with multiple eligible wallet items.
steps.expected_result: The order details page lists the eligible items.

steps.action: Click the Add to Wallet action.
steps.expected_result: A multi-item selection or multi-pass wallet flow is shown when supported; the flow is not limited to a single hardcoded item.

steps.action: Select one item and start the wallet save flow.
steps.expected_result: The provider flow opens with pass data for the selected item only.

steps.action: Repeat with all eligible items or the Add entire order option when supported.
steps.expected_result: Each selected pass is created for the correct item without duplicates or cross-item data.

steps.action: Review the saved passes.
steps.expected_result: Each pass shows the correct item/order details.

cases.title: Core - User - My Orders - NFC - Add multiple NFC tickets to digital wallet
cases.description: Verify that a logged-in buyer can add wallet passes for multiple eligible NFC tickets from an NFC-enabled order detail page.
cases.preconditions:
A logged-in buyer has an order with multiple NFC pass-only tickets.
The NFC tickets are eligible for wallet access and are not transferred or listed for resale.
Use a compatible Apple Wallet or Google Wallet context.
cases.postconditions: The buyer can save the intended NFC wallet passes and the order remains accessible from My Orders.

steps.action: Open the order details page for the NFC order.
steps.expected_result: The order details page lists the NFC tickets.

steps.action: Verify the NFC ticket access state before starting the wallet flow.
steps.expected_result: The page does not expose a static PDF ticket download for NFC pass-only tickets.

steps.action: Click the Add to Wallet action.
steps.expected_result: The NFC wallet flow or multi-ticket selection modal opens when supported.

steps.action: Select one NFC ticket and start the provider save flow.
steps.expected_result: The wallet provider flow opens with data for the selected NFC ticket.

steps.action: Repeat for another NFC ticket or use the supported multi-pass option.
steps.expected_result: Each selected NFC pass is created for the correct ticket without exposing another ticket's barcode data.

cases.title: Core - Orders - Verify Date Accuracy on Ticket Custom Start Date
cases.description:
Validates that the receipt PDF and digital wallet passes (Apple and Google) correctly display either the event's start date or the ticket type's custom start date override. This covers single-day events, recurring events, and various configuration states including fallbacks for missing or invalid data.

Experiment with TT having different start dates.
cases.preconditions:
* An event exists with a defined start date/time.
* A ticket type is created with the configuration specified in the \`OverrideType\` parameter.

steps.action: Navigate to the event page for the specified \`EventOccurrence\` and purchase a ticket of the type defined by \`OverrideType\`.
steps.expected_result: Purchase is completed successfully.

steps.action: Open the Order Confirmation and download the Receipt PDF.
steps.expected_result: If \`OverrideType\` is \`CustomStart\`, the PDF shows the custom date. For all other values, it falls back to the event's start date.

steps.action: Click "Add to Google Wallet" on the confirmation page or from the email.
steps.expected_result: The Google Wallet pass displays the date corresponding to the \`OverrideType\` logic (Custom date or Event fallback).

steps.action: Click "Add to Apple Wallet" on the confirmation page or from the email.
steps.expected_result: The Apple Wallet pass displays the date corresponding to the \`OverrideType\` logic (Custom date or Event fallback).

cases.title: Ticket Transfer Date Consistency
cases.description: This test ensures that the custom date configuration remains attached to a ticket during the transfer process between users. It validates that the recipient receives a wallet pass with the same custom date as the original ticket, maintaining data integrity through the secondary ownership flow.
cases.preconditions: - User A owns a ticket with a custom start date configuration.

steps.action: User A initiates a transfer of the ticket to User B
steps.expected_result: The transfer invitation is sent.

steps.action: User B accepts the transfer and views the ticket in their account
steps.expected_result: The ticket displays the original custom start date.

steps.action: User B adds the ticket to their Google or Apple Wallet
steps.expected_result: The wallet pass displays the correct custom start date.

cases.title: Dashboard - Branding - Digital Wallet Branding Management Flow
cases.description: Validates the complete lifecycle of digital wallet branding for a venue. This includes initial form loading, customization of colors and primary images, validation of asset constraints, persistence of advanced branding assets, recovery from save failures, and the removal of existing customizations. This test ensures the branding interface remains functional and accurately reflects the organizer's configuration in the digital pass preview.
cases.preconditions: - User is logged in as an employee with manage event permissions.
cases.postconditions: - Customization is saved and applied to digital wallet.

steps.action: Open the Dashboard menu → Settings → Organization Info → Branding → Deliverables → Digital Wallets.
steps.expected_result: Skeletons appear during load. Once loaded, Colors, Images, and Advanced Images sections render. Live preview shows fallback colors and "Your Brand". No "Remove" action is visible.

steps.action: Modify Background, Foreground, and Label colors in the Colors section and click Save
steps.expected_result: A success notification appears and the live preview updates to reflect the new colors.

steps.action: Upload a Logo, Icon, and Strip image in the Images section and click Save
steps.expected_result: Upload previews appear. The pass preview reflects the new assets. A success notification appears and assets persist after a page reload.

steps.action: Upload unsupported file types or files exceeding size/dimension limits to any image field
steps.expected_result: The field displays the specific validation error (e.g., "File too large") and the invalid asset is not saved.

steps.action: Expand the Advanced Images section, upload all available assets, and click Save
steps.expected_result: A success notification appears and all advanced assets persist after a page reload.
steps.data: Google Wallet Logo, Artwork, Venue Map, Stacked View Logo, Secondary Logo

steps.action: Simulate a network or server failure and attempt to Save a section
steps.expected_result: An error notification appears; the form is not locked and remains interactive.

steps.action: Resolve the failure and click Save again
steps.expected_result: The save operation succeeds and a success notification is displayed.

steps.action: Click the Remove action and confirm the removal in the modal
steps.expected_result: A confirmation modal titled "Remove digital wallet customization" appears. After confirming, a success notification appears and the page reverts to default preview values.

cases.title: Core - User - Wallet - Verify Apple and Google Wallet pass update lifecycle
cases.description: Verifies that generated wallet passes can be registered or tokenized and later receive updated ticket data after supported ticket, event, or venue wallet customization changes.
cases.preconditions:
- Buyer has a wallet-capable ticket or membership.
- Apple Wallet registration or Google Wallet token test path is available.
- Organizer can update wallet-affecting event or branding data in the test environment.
cases.postconditions:
- Wallet pass/object data reflects the latest supported ticket, event, or branding state.
- No duplicate stale pass remains for the same ticket after update.

steps.action: Generate or add the selected item to the selected wallet provider.
steps.expected_result: Wallet pass/object is generated successfully.

steps.action: Open the generated pass and record the initial event, ticket, barcode/pass, and branding details.
steps.expected_result: Initial pass data matches the purchased item.

steps.action: Update a supported wallet-affecting field such as event display data, ticket state, or venue wallet branding.
steps.expected_result: Wallet-affecting update is saved in Showpass.

steps.action: Trigger or wait for wallet pass regeneration/update.
steps.expected_result: Pass update process completes without an error.

steps.action: Open or refresh the wallet pass again.
steps.expected_result: Wallet pass shows the updated supported data and does not show stale duplicate details.
